findings.note: stillPresentKind.Decode is the only kind Decode that skips checkPayload, on the comment 'MaxDeltaList statuses of MaxShort ids always fit the payload'. The arithmetic is false: 256 statuses whose ids are at the MaxShort cap (1024 B) canonicalize to roughly 256*1070 = 274 KB, over MaxPayload-envelopeMargin (262016 B). It is reachable: cmd nodes may contribute Confirmed bugs with ids up to MaxShort each, split across iterations so each individual delta stays under the payload cap while AllFound grows to the 256-bug cliff. stillPresentExec then emits an oversized statusOut that Decode accepts and the node_output append rejects at run/fold.go:43 (ReasonOversize), surfacing as a raw ERR_APPEND_REJECTED from machine.go rather than the intended ERR_TOO_MANY_BUGS / node-output-invalid gate. Contrived but the stated invariant is simply wrong; either cap ids tighter or call checkPayload here too.

findings.note: New applies the Mock invariant unconditionally: with Judge nil, isMock is false, so Deps{Judge: nil, Mock: true} is refused. Spec 5 r4 states the invariant 'still checks isMock != d.Mock only when a judge is present'. The divergence is on the safe side and no current caller hits it (cli/wiring.go:189 and cli/run.go:233 are consistent by construction), so this is a spec-wording/implementation mismatch to reconcile, not a behavioural bug.

adjudicateExec's match phase issues one judge call per (golden, candidate) pair with no spend or call ceiling: with MaxGoldens 64 and up to 256 deduplicated candidates that is up to 16,384 billed calls in a single node, and nothing in machine or fold enforces a token/call budget. The pre-flight only bounds output size, not spend. This was already logged as an architecture advisory ('match O(g x c) unbounded') for the spec, and the implementation inherits it; recording it here so the advisory is not lost, not as a new blocker.

findings.note: lensCount silently falls back to all 8 lenses whenever Params['lenses'] is not a Go int. Today YAML parsing yields int and validateLenses rejects anything else at parse time, so the fallback is unreachable through workflow.Parse - but only because Options.Kinds carries ValidateParams. Any loader that builds a Node without the kind registry's KindInfo (or a future JSON/var-substituted params path, where a number decodes as float64 or a substituted var becomes a string) would silently review with 8 lenses instead of erroring. A typed lookup that distinguishes 'absent' from 'wrong type' would remove the trap.
